\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Hybrid Deployment Pattern: tier-conditioned explainer recommendation.}

\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{p{2.0cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.0cm} X}
\toprule
\textbf{Tier} & \textbf{Recommendation} & \textbf{Evidence and recommended condition} \\
\midrule
Tier 1: Real-Time / End-User &
Model-architecture-conditioned: \textbf{SHAP} (\texttt{TreeExplainer}) for
XGBoost; \textbf{LIME} for non-tree/black-box models (neural networks,
opaque APIs); for other tree ensembles, measure latency before choosing. &
For XGBoost, \texttt{TreeExplainer} was faster than LIME in all 15 matched
cells (median 18.1~ms vs.\ 61.8~ms), so SHAP is simultaneously faster
\emph{and} more faithful and the usual fidelity--latency trade-off does
not apply. This does not hold for tree models in general: for random
forests, \texttt{TreeExplainer} was slower in all 15 cells (median
1,262.4~ms vs.\ 335.6~ms), since its $O(TLD)$ cost grows with the number
and depth of the trees. For non-tree
models, LIME's lower median runtime (53.3~ms vs.\ 694.6~ms for
KernelSHAP; Figure~2) gives a latency
advantage where sampling is the only option. Recommended when sub-second
latency and compact explanations matter more than maximizing fidelity
and no fast model-aware explainer is available. \\[6pt]
Tier 2: Auditing / Data Science &
\textbf{SHAP.} &
Use for bias analysis, model debugging, or regulatory inquiries: consistent
paired advantages in stability, fidelity, and faithfulness gap ($d_z =
3.00$, $4.82$, $2.63$). Recommended for analyst-mediated or offline
workflows tolerating second-to-minute latency; plan sample budgets
according to whether SHAP runs in tree-specific or kernel mode. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}
